name: Administrative assistants and executive assistants
oneLiner: Scheduling, drafting and coordinating: the tasks AI does most, in the occupation group that accounts for 42% of the fall in young workers.
why: Trust and discretion still matter: the assistant knows things the org chart does not
Someone must coordinate people who will not coordinate themselves
threats: Scheduling, drafting and coordinating are the activities that appear most in records of real AI use
The entry rung is the part that closed: firms are not replacing assistants, they are not hiring them

claims.text: Administrative assistants appear among the roles employers expect to decline sharply to 2030 — an expectation, not an observed count.
The most common and most successful AI-assisted activities are information work — creating, processing and communicating information.
The ILO's refined index places clerical support work in the highest exposure gradients.

Occupations whose AI exposure rose most between the first half of 2023 and the first half of 2026 show no change in total employment or unemployment, but about 8% fewer workers under 30 for each standard deviation of the rise.

Office and administrative support accounts for 42% of that under-30 decline while employing 13% of young workers; secretaries and administrative assistants are among the occupations contributing 5 to 8% of the young-worker loss in the most exposed quartile, behind customer service representatives at 35%.

Job-finding rates fell about six points more in the most AI-exposed occupations than in the least exposed between the 2015–2019 baseline and 2024–2026, while separation rates showed no consistent relationship with exposure.
The implied unemployment gap between least and most exposed occupations is about two points for workers aged 23–30, against at most one point for workers aged 45–54.
